method: strict live no-kb vs prompt-contained with-kb comparison; shared broken RTL, isolated work branches; each round patches only concrete current SpyGlass file/line/tag findings and reruns SpyGlass until 0 errors / 0 warnings or concrete blocker
per_round_budget: 100-200 modules or 1200-2500 changed lines, unless the current report has fewer local fixes left

with_kb.wall_seconds_source: about 25 minutes from first counted patch timestamp 20260704_143813 to final result timestamp 20260704_150326
kb_excerpts_used: sim_race02 / W415: multiple drivers and same-cycle multiple assignments

comparison.wall_clock_note: no-kb uses metrics timestamp wall seconds; with-kb reports approximate wall clock string, so wall-clock comparison is directional only.

measurement_gaps: analysis_seconds and edit_seconds were required by the method but were not consistently instrumented by the two workers in this 10000 run.
with-kb JSON records analysis_seconds/edit_seconds as null and lint_seconds per round.
no-kb JSON records per-round E/W/I metrics and aggregate lint/wall time, but not per-round analysis/edit durations.
Therefore the cleanest quantitative comparison here is natural round count and recorded MCP lint wall time, with wall-clock as approximate/contextual.
interpretation: Both arms started from the same broken RTL and independently reached actual 0 errors / 0 warnings.
With the enlarged per-round cap, the prompt-contained KB excerpt did not produce a speed advantage in this run: no-kb completed in 14 rounds and with-kb in 15 counted rounds.
Recorded MCP lint time was effectively equal: no-kb 568.01s vs with-kb 576.6854s, a 1.5% difference in favor of no-kb.

This suggests the larger per-round budget let no-kb amortize lack of KB by patching broad report-local patterns; KB guidance may matter more under smaller per-round budgets or when root-cause ambiguity is higher.
